candidate_spec.high_level_variant: Maintain same map and mission but bring the slower linear actor closer into the ego’s lane at low relative speed to ensure a short-distance interaction and likely contact while planning still produces non-blocked final waypoints.
candidate_spec.mutation_intent: Tighten proximity between ego and a single slow-moving actor directly ahead/alongside, increasing the chance of contact while preserving the pattern: another actor within a few meters, active perception/prediction, available non-blocked final waypoints, and ambiguous ego actuation versus motion history.
pre_execution_validation_rules: Ensure at least one non-ego actor (e.g., index 0 or 1) is spawned within 5 m Euclidean distance of the ego trajectory within the last 5 s before the planned end of the run.
Verify that perception detection topics (e.g., /detection/objects) contain at least one object in the 5 s window preceding any potential collision time.
Verify that prediction topics (e.g., /prediction/objects) are published and contain at least one predicted object in the same window.
Confirm that planning final waypoints are non-empty and structurally valid (e.g., ~O(100) points) throughout the scenario with no global failure before the anticipated collision window.
post_execution_validation_rules: Check the oracle or simulator logs for a collision event involving the ego and a non-ego actor (index 0 or 1), not just a near-miss.
Compute the minimum distance between ego and each non-ego actor in the 5 s window before collision; require at least one to be within 3 m shortly before impact.

Confirm that final waypoints remain available and non-null (similar count as earlier in the run) up to within 1 s of the collision time, with no global ‘blocked’ or emergency-stop flags dominating the final rows.
Verify that perception and prediction topics contain at least one object in the 3 s before collision; do not require that the specific colliding actor be conclusively matched.

Inspect vehicle command and vehicle status traces: allow inconsistency (e.g., zero throttle commands while ego speed is nonzero) and do not reject the case solely for such discrepancies, to preserve attribution uncertainty.
uncertainty: The exact mechanism of contact (which actor moves into whom, and whether the ego is nominally stopped) is left unconstrained to maintain ambiguity.
No explicit guarantee is imposed that the colliding actor is the same as any perceived object, only that at least one object exists in detection/prediction streams.
Actuation and vehicle-status consistency is intentionally not enforced, so root-cause localization can remain uncertain between planning, control, and simulation artifacts.
